title: Hang a framed picture on a wall hook by the wire behind it, level, then let go
instruction: Hang the picture on the wall hook by its wire so it hangs straight, then let go.
context: Hanging a picture is one of the most familiar jobs in any home. Ability tested: carrying a wide, flat frame upright with two hands and landing its hidden wire on a hook by feel. The wire is behind the frame, so the frame is lowered until the slack wire drops over the hook. A wire caught off-centre hangs crooked; a push on a lower corner levels it. Held by one side alone, the frame swings round the grip.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases (x forward, y left); heights above the table. Wall: a white 12 mm MDF panel, 90 wide x 60 tall, standing on the table along y, its face at x 45, held by two steel shelf brackets clamped to the table. Hook: one 30 lb nail-in steel picture hook (OOK/Hillman type: 13 x 32 mm plate, lip 12 mm out) at y 0, its throat 39 cm up. Picture: a black plastic poster frame 30 wide x 40 tall (outer), 25 x 22 mm moulding, styrene glazing, hardboard back, 0.2 kg, centred at y 0, standing on its bottom edge on the table and leaning back 25 degrees on the panel, face to the robot, its top just below the hook. On its back, two D-rings 10 cm below the top, 2 cm in from each side, with 1.5 mm braided picture wire, 27 cm between the rings, so hung its peak is about 6 cm below the top. Arms start in the ready pose, grippers open.
scoring: Tools: the trial video, a ruler and a level pencil line drawn on the panel 50 cm up. Judged 2 s after the robot stops. Score 0 if the frame rests on the table (lowest corner within 5 mm of it), if any gripper is within 5 mm of it, or if it does not hang from the hook by its wire alone (wire lying in the hook's throat). Otherwise 1.0 when the two top corners differ in height by less than 1.0 cm (2 degrees over 30 cm; ruler from the pencil line), the bottom rail is within 1 cm of the panel, and both grippers are at least 5 cm from the frame. Hanging from the hook by its wire but with the corners 1.0 cm or more apart, the bottom rail more than 1 cm off the panel, or a gripper between 5 mm and 5 cm from the frame: 0.5. Example 0.5 end states: wire caught 2 cm off-centre so the frame hangs crooked; hung level with a gripper left 2 cm away.
reset_notes: Lift the picture off the hook and stand it back on its bottom edge at y 0, leaning on the panel at 25 degrees (bottom edge at x 26, use a tape mark on the table), wire hanging loose behind it. The hook is never moved.
fidelity: Frame: one rigid box, real size and mass. Wire: chain of 2 cm rigid segments, 3 mm thick and 60 g (real: 1.5 mm, a few g) for stable contact, bending springs, no stretch or twist; each end is a short 30 g stub (the twisted-back end) held in its D-ring by a stiff spring (about 3 mm give hung, the same at both ends). Hook: fixed rigid shape (its nail holds 30 lb), friction 0.4, so a wire caught off-centre can leave the frame crooked. Panel and table rigid.
